transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... lately, things have just been feeling off. The school district recently decided to put this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate, right on top of my regular teaching duties. I mean, I still get through the day and do my job, but I just feel so wound up and discouraged. It's really not like me. I've even started putting off my lesson plans and ignoring emails that I used to handle without a second thought. It's just getting to be a bit much to manage.
Did these feelings begin after the district assigned you the new rollout?

Yes, it definitely started after that. I'd say I started feeling unlike myself within the first month or two after they added that rollout to my full teaching load. Before they made that change, I was managing my usual work and commitments pretty well. It just feels like it tipped the scales.
What do you find yourself worrying about most these days?

I'm not really sure if there's one specific thing I worry about the most. It's more of just a general feeling of being overwhelmed. I guess I just worry about getting it all done, but there isn't really a specific fear or anything like that. It's just a lot to handle all at once.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad. Um, definitely not all day or anything like that. It's really just that overwhelmed, stressed feeling I mentioned. I don't feel down in the dumps... just frustrated by how much is on my plate right now.
Do you feel noticeably anxious or nervous because of the added workload?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious or nervous. Um, I don't feel jittery or anything like that. It really is just that heavy, stressed feeling of having too much to do and not enough time to do it, rather than actually feeling nervous.
